rules.statement: A method that produces output whose length the caller cannot know in advance (such as an unwrapped or decrypted key) writes into a caller-supplied `IBufferWriter<byte>`, advances the writer only on success, and zeroes whatever it wrote if it fails.
rules.why: The caller cannot size a buffer up front, and secret material written partway through a failed operation must not stay in the caller's buffer.
rules.check: Look for unwrap/decrypt APIs that return newly allocated `byte[]` for secret output, or that call `Advance` before the operation has succeeded, or that leave partial secret bytes behind on an exception path without clearing them.

rules.statement: A public producer that writes to a caller-supplied buffer or `IBufferWriter<T>` comes with a public sizing method (such as `GetXxxLength`/`GetByteCount`) next to it, so callers can size the destination.
rules.why: Under the buffer-operations convention, the sizing method sits beside the writer-based producer so callers can pre-size buffers without guessing.
rules.check: Look for new span- or writer-based `Write`/`Wrap`/`Decode` methods that have no matching length or byte-count method on the same type.

rules.statement: A refactor or rename of types must not rename configuration keys and sections, persisted column names, stored identifiers, or operator-facing setting names. Keep the existing external names even when the code types change name.
rules.why: Renaming them changes configuration and stored data, which a refactor must not do.
rules.check: In a diff described as a rename or refactor, look for changed configuration section/key strings, options binding paths, database column names, or persisted constant values.

rules.statement: When a role is filled by selecting one registered implementation by name from configuration, do not add a marker interface for that role. Select from all implementations of the base contract through a catalog.
rules.why: Any registered implementation can fill the role, so a marker interface adds a type without adding a rule.
rules.check: Look for new empty interfaces that derive from an existing contract only to mark a configurable role (e.g. `IRootXxx : IXxx` with no members).

rules.statement: Put a contract in the package that matches its concern, and keep BCL-only cryptographic or key-material contracts out of persistence packages so consumers don't have to take a persistence dependency to use them.
rules.why: Wrapping a key has nothing to do with persisted data contracts, and a contract in a persistence package forces unrelated consumers to depend on persistence.
rules.check: Look for new interfaces or DTOs added to a `*.Persistence.*` package that have no persistence concern and need only the BCL.

rules.statement: Name vendor adapter packages `<contract area>.<Vendor>`, after the contract they implement and not after an unrelated area such as persistence.
rules.why: The family names an adapter by its contract area plus vendor (e.g. `NCode.Identity.SharedState.Valkey`), and an adapter named after the wrong area misleads consumers.
rules.check: Look for new adapter projects or namespaces whose middle segment names a different area from the contract the adapter implements.

rules.statement: Decode stored base64url key ciphertext with the shared strict decoder (built on `NCode.Base64Url`, which refuses padding and illegal characters). Throw `CryptographicException` for empty or invalid text and `ArgumentException` for a destination that is too short; don't hand-roll a decoder in each wrapper.
rules.why: With one decoder, every wrapper refuses malformed ciphertext with the same exception and message.
rules.check: Look for key wrapper or KMS adapter code that calls `Convert.FromBase64String`, does its own base64url translation, or accepts padded input when decoding wrapped-key ciphertext.
